title: Geometrical Constructions
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 8; not yet checked by a Kenyan maths teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Official outcomes a to g are tested; h (use IT) and i (admire patterns) are not questions. Constructions are done on paper with a ruler and compasses (a protractor for polygon angles); a phone question can only test the plan, the reason for a step or a length that follows, so most construction skills are tested that way and the drawing itself is for the teacher to see. Two families with Grade 9 ids (g9.construct.polygon-angle, g9.construct.circum-centre) carry Grade 8 outcomes and are filed here. One family asks for either the circle through the corners or the circle touching the sides; it is filed under f. Parallel and perpendicular lines (a), regular and irregular polygons (d, e) and the inscribed circle (g) have no family yet. Teacher to confirm: whether learners are expected to know that the centre of the circle through a right-angled triangle's corners is the midpoint of the hypotenuse.

skills.key_step: The child keeps the compass radius the same for the two arcs that must cross, and says why: the crossing is the same distance from both points.

floor.question: How do you find the middle of AB with compasses?
floor.answer: equal arcs from A and B, join the crossings

contexts: a fence parallel to a road

board.do: Draw a line AB and a point P above it.
Point at P.
board.say: With the compass point on P, what do we draw first?

board.do: Wait for the child to say an arc cutting AB twice.
The child draws the next two equal arcs.

misconceptions.ask: How do we know the angle is exactly 90 degrees?
Why must the arcs be the same?
Does it pass through P?
Is P above the middle of AB?

checks.question: First step to draw a perpendicular from P to AB?
checks.answer: with centre P, draw an arc cutting AB at two points

checks.question: Why must the two arcs below AB have the same radius?
checks.answer: so the crossing is the same distance from both points

skills.key_step: The child adds the ratio numbers to get the equal parts on the ray and joins the last mark to the far end.

floor.prerequisite: Adds the parts of a ratio.
floor.question: 2 : 3: parts altogether

representations: a ray with equal compass steps
lines parallel to the last join
steps: Step off (a + b) equal parts with compasses.
Join the last mark to B.
Draw a parallel line through mark a.
contexts: sharing a boundary between two plots
a map line in a ratio

board.do: Draw AB and a ray from A.
Point at the ray.
board.say: For 2 : 3, how many equal steps do we mark?

board.do: Wait for 5.
The child joins the fifth mark to B and draws the parallel through mark 2.

misconceptions.ask: Do we add or multiply the parts?
Where does the 3 part go?
Where does the 2 part go?
What do the parallel lines do to AB?
Do parallel lines make right angles with AB?
misconceptions.repair: They copy the slope of the join.

misconceptions.ask: What do the parallel lines carry to AB?

checks.question: To divide a line in the ratio 3 : 4, how many equal parts on the ray?
Which mark is joined to B?

skills.key_step: The child finds one part (length ÷ total parts) and then each piece from the named end.
steps: Match the first number to the first end.

board.do: Draw a 15 cm line AB in 5 equal parts.
Point at one part.
Wait for 3 cm.
Ask: how long is the piece next to A for 2 : 3?

misconceptions.ask: Is taking 5 away sharing into 5?
Can a part be longer than the line?
Which number goes with A?
Is that the part or the whole?

checks.question: A 21 cm line is divided in the ratio 3 : 4 from A. Part next to A?
A 24 cm line in the ratio 1 : 5. Longer part?

skills.key_step: The child splits the polygon into triangles from one corner to get the sum, then shares it for a regular polygon.

floor.prerequisite: Knows angles in a triangle add to 180°.
floor.question: Angle sum of a triangle

representations: a table of n, sum, one angle

board.do: Draw a pentagon and the diagonals from one corner.
Count the triangles with the child.
Point at the three triangles.
board.say: What do all the angles add to?

board.do: Wait for 540°.

misconceptions.ask: Is 72 inside or outside the corner?
One angle or all six?
How many triangles in a pentagon?
How many right angles in 720°?
Walking round, how much do you turn?

checks.question: Interior angle of a regular octagon?
Angle sum of a heptagon (7 sides)?

skills.key_step: The child decides the angle to construct (at each corner or at the centre) and keeps every side the same length.

floor.prerequisite: Finds the interior angle of a regular polygon.
floor.question: Regular pentagon

representations: a circle cut into equal sectors
steps: Mark equal angles at the centre (360° ÷ n), or step the radius round for a hexagon.
contexts: a pentagon badge for a club

board.do: Draw a circle of radius 4 cm.
Point at the rim.
board.say: If we step 4 cm round the rim with compasses, how many steps fit?

board.do: Wait for the child to predict.
The child steps round and joins the marks.

misconceptions.ask: Are all its angles equal?
Is 72° at the centre or the corner?
What shape is each slice of the hexagon?
What do the angles at the centre add to?

checks.question: Angle at the centre between two corners of a regular pentagon?
A regular hexagon is drawn in a circle of radius 5 cm. Side?

skills.key_step: The child sketches and labels the polygon before drawing, and builds it side by side in the order of the letters.

floor.prerequisite: Constructs a triangle from two sides and an angle.
floor.question: AB 5 cm, angle A 60°, AC 4 cm: first step?

steps: Angle at each corner, then the next side.
contexts: a plan of an irregular plot

board.do: Sketch quadrilateral ABCD with AB 5 cm, angle B 90°, BC 4 cm.
Point at B.
board.say: Which angle is made at this corner?

board.do: Wait for angle ABC.
The child constructs 90° at B and marks BC.

misconceptions.ask: Which side starts at B?
Which letter is in the middle of ABC?
Does the last side match?
Is the angle smaller or bigger than a right angle?

checks.question: In ABCDE, which corner has angle CDE?
After drawing AB and the angle at B, what is marked next?

skills.key_step: The child says the centre must be the same distance from all three corners, so it lies on the perpendicular bisectors.

floor.question: Where is the middle of a 10 cm line?

steps: Bisect two sides at right angles.
The meeting point is the centre.
Right-angled triangle: centre at the middle of the longest side.
contexts: a water tank to serve three homes
a round fence through three trees

board.do: Draw a triangle ABC.
The child bisects AB and BC at right angles.
Point at the meeting point.
board.say: How far is it from A, B and C?

board.do: Wait for the child to say the same.

misconceptions.ask: Is the longest side the radius or the diameter?
Where is the centre for a right-angled triangle?
Which side is the diameter?
Same distance from the corners or the sides?
Is that point the same distance from each corner?
Where does it cross AB?
Does drawing lines change the triangle?
What do we need the meeting point for?

checks.question: A right-angled triangle has sides 5, 12 and 13 cm. Radius of the circle through its corners?
Which lines find the centre of the circle through the corners?
checks.answer: the perpendicular bisectors of two sides

skills.key_step: The child says the centre must be the same distance from all three sides, so it lies on the angle bisectors, and measures the radius at a right angle to a side.

floor.question: How do you bisect angle A?
floor.answer: equal arcs on the arms, then arcs from those points; join to A

steps: The meeting point is the centre.
Construct the perpendicular from it to a side.
contexts: the biggest round tank in a triangular plot
a round mat in a corner

board.do: Draw a triangle ABC.
The child bisects angles A and B.
Point at the meeting point.
board.say: How do we find the radius from here?

board.do: Wait for the child to say a perpendicular to a side.

misconceptions.ask: Does the circle pass through the corners?
Is every triangle equilateral?
misconceptions.repair: It touches at the foot of the perpendicular.

misconceptions.ask: Which line to the side is shortest?
Where on that line is the centre?
misconceptions.repair: Where a second bisector meets it.

checks.question: Which lines find the centre of the circle touching the sides of a triangle?
How is its radius found?
checks.answer: the perpendicular distance from the centre to a side
